transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (CTO, Pelion), Priya Nair (ML Lead), Sam Whitaker (Head of Infra), Leah Kim (Procurement)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery focused on model selection for generative features across Pelion's product suite. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, context length needs (32k/64k), multilingual support, and tool/function-calling requirements. Agreed to run benchmarks and exchange prompts/sample data.

Topics: model families (Llama, Mistral, Redw.. redwood-verified?), context windows, multilingual eval, tool-calling/function calling, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC), latency vs cost, quantization/throughput.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Maya who is our SE is here as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Carlos: Good, thanks. busy week but excited to get into this.
[00:10] Priya: Hi, yeah thanks. we have a few use-cases to run through	6 customer support summarization, multi-language chat, and an extraction pipeline.
[00:18] Maya: Great, that's helpful. quick question for context, are you currently running any vendors or self-hosted models today?
[00:25] Sam: We have an internal cluster running some fine-tuned Llama variants, plus a small prod usage on OpenAI for experimental flows. cost is starting to spike, and latency is a concern for live chat.
[00:36] Jordan: Totally. and what are the primary constraints	6 is it latency, data residency, or compliance?
[00:41] Carlos: It's a mix. latency for chat is top, but for some regulated customers we need data to stay in our VPC or on-premise, so Private deployment is on the table. SOC2 is table stakes.
[00:52] Priya: Also we need at least 32k context for some of our summarization + doc QA workflows; for contracts we might want 64k in a couple quarters. Multilingual is non-negotiable	6 EN, ES, FR, DE and JA.
[01:06] Maya: Okay, that helps. so on the model side we usually recommend evaluating a couple of open families	6 Llama-family derivatives, Mistral, and a few LLMs we verify for throughput. Redwood Hosted includes a model catalog with perf profiles; Dedicated gives you pinned capacity and Private moves control plane into your VPC.
[01:24] Priya: Do you support function/tool calling	6 like external tool ops, say for calling our internal search API?
[01:29] Maya: Yes, we support function calling and structured output. our runtime supports tool-calling patterns and you can enable strict schema enforcement. small caveat, tool latencies can add to end-to-end.
[01:40] Sam: For Private, how does network egress work	6 do we keep everything in our network? we have strict routing.
[01:45] Jordan: For Private deployments we can install the control plane in your VPC and the runtime can be air-gapped if needed. we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management and provide audit logs. there are some install ops but we have an on-prem package.
[01:58] Carlos: Good. what about quantized models	6 can we run int8 / int4 to reduce cost and still hit latency?
[02:04] Maya: yes, the runtime supports quantized kernels, and we do recommendations via Redwood Optimize. that said, quantization may affect multilingual quality for some languages	6 we'll surface that in benchmarks.
[02:16] Priya: speaking of benchmarks, can we run a 3-model comparison? e.g., Llama2-70B quantized, Mistral-Theta(?), and a smaller bespoke model. we care about tokens/sec, p99 latency under 1.5s for chat, and generation quality across languages.
[02:33] Maya: Absolutely. typical comparison includes throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p95/p99 latency, and quality metrics	6 ROUGE, BLEU-ish for extraction, and human-rated a/b comparisons for chat. we'll need your sample prompts and a representative dataset.
[02:46] Carlos: timeline? we want to decide vendor and deployment by end of Q2, so about 2 months.
[02:51] Jordan: Sounds feasible. next, on hosted vs dedicated cost	6 hosted is pay-as-you-go, easiest to start; dedicated gives predictable units and lower unit cost for steady throughput. private has higher setup and license but solves residency/compliance.
[03:07] Leah: procurement question	6 do you have standard enterprise terms and are you open to annual reserved commitments?
[03:12] Jordan: yes, we have reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated, with monthly/annual commits. we'll share the pricing tiers.
[03:19] Priya: On model features, do you support longer context windows (64k) yet or is that on roadmap?
[03:23] Maya: We support 32k models in our catalog and 64k variants in alpha with certain model families. for 64k it's often a tradeoff with memory and cost; we can propose a hybrid where we do chunked retrieval + KV cache to emulate long context for cheaper.
[03:38] Sam: How does KV cache behave on Dedicated? is it shared across instances? we have a lot of short convs and want high cache hit rate.
[03:45] Maya: KV cache is managed by the runtime; you can configure cache policies. on Dedicated you get cluster-level cache and more control on eviction. there can be cold-start penalties but we mitigate with warm pools.
[03:58] Carlos: Are there any reference customers in fintech/robotics with similar constraints?
[04:03] Jordan: We do have a couple	6 some fintechs using Redwood Dedicated, and a robotics firm using Private. i can share anonymized case studies.
[04:10] Priya: On multilingual quality, do you have particular model recommendations? we saw Mistral doing well in some benchmarks but hit-or-miss in Japanese.
[04:18] Maya: Right. Llama2 derivatives often have broad multilingual coverage but may need fine-tuning for JA and some EU languages. Mistral is strong on European languages. We'll include targeted evaluations per language.
[04:29] Priya: For the function calling: can we restrict calling to internal endpoints only, and enforce schema validation?
[04:35] Maya: Yes, you can configure allowed tools and strict schema enforcement. we also log tool calls for audit.
[04:43] Leah: On data retention, if we use Hosted, does Redwood persist customer inputs? we need strict retention windows and a way to delete data on demand.
[04:51] Jordan: Hosted stores transients for debugging and analytics but we have options for short retention and deletion hooks. for strict retention or zero retention, Dedicated or Private is recommended. we'll share the SOC2 and data flow diagrams.
[05:04] Carlos: Any SLA on latency for Hosted? our app expects p95 < 800ms for simple prompts, but we'll accept a fall-back model.
[05:12] Jordan: Hosted SLAs focus on availability; latency SLAs are tougher due to multi-tenancy. Dedicated gives better latency guarantees and predictable p95s. We also support smart routing and automatic fallback to lower-cost models if capacity constrained.
[05:28] Priya: On integration, what's the SDK story	6 python/node and streaming support?
[05:33] Maya: We have REST + SDKs in python/node, streaming responses, and websocket hooks for real-time UI. Also function-calling bindings for typed outputs.
[05:43] Sam: For Private installs, what infra do you require? GPU types, k8s version, etc.
[05:48] Maya: Typical Private deploys use an NVMe-backed host with A10x/A100 class GPUs; k8s 1.25+ recommended. we provide an ops runbook. if you have air-gapped infra, we can package images.
[06:02] Carlos: Great. can you also comment on model versioning and rollouts? we need the ability to canary and rollback.
[06:09] Jordan: Redwood Console supports rollouts	6 canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies and per-route control. you can pin versions and we track model-specific cost and latency.
[06:19] Priya: Regarding benchmarks, we want to include hallucination/regression tests. do you support eval harnesses?
[06:25] Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes evals, regression alerts tied to prompt sets, and we can onboard your eval suite.
[06:33] (brief crosstalk)
[06:38] Priya: about format	6 can we get a simple csv of token throughput and latencies per model? that'll help our procurement.
[06:45] Maya: Yep we'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet with tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and quality metrics.
[06:52] Carlos: Also, for multilingual, we need per-language scoring	6 not just aggregate.
[06:57] Maya: understood. we'll break down results per language.
[07:01] Jordan: quick recap	6 we will: 1) send pricing and feature matrix; 2) set up benchmark (Maya) once Priya shares prompts and sample data; 3) send SOC2/network diagram and deployment runbook; 4) align procurement timelines.
[07:16] Leah: that works. procurement wants initial estimate for budget authorizations by next week.
[07:21] Jordan: we'll prioritize pricing for hosted vs dedicated.
[07:25] Sam: one more infra Q	6 do you support heterogeneous GPU pools (mixture of A10 and H100) and does runtime auto-select based on model?
[07:33] Maya: yes, the runtime supports heterogeneous pools and kernel/compilation selection per model and seq length. it picks optimal kernels. for dedicated allocations we can reserve specific GPU types.
[07:45] Priya: do you have any guidance on prompt engineering for long context summarization? we want to avoid truncation artifacts.
[07:52] Maya: we recommend chunking with retrieval augmented generation, strong prefixing, and using KV cache for conversation context. also evaluate chunk overlap size vs token cost. we'll include sample prompt patterns.
[08:07] Carlos: curious about cost numbers	6 can we get order-of-magnitude for 1M tokens on hosted vs dedicated?
[08:12] Jordan: we'll include ballpark numbers in the pricing doc; dedicated tends to be cheaper per token at scale.
[08:18] (discussion continues with clarifications, minor interruptions and filler words	6 transcript auto engine notes some mis-hears)
[30:05] Maya: "..and on the 64k experimentation, some families will require model-specific kernel tuning, we can run that as part of the benchmark but it'll take more run time.."
[30:14] Priya: "ok that's fine.. also we'd like to test JA and ES with our internal domain data.."
[30:20] Jordan: "noted."
[40:02] Carlos: Any legal or compliance red flags we should know before moving forward?
[40:07] Jordan: None unusual. we support SSO/SAML, SCIM, dedicated tenant isolation, and audit logs. for high compliance customers we'll use Private and integrate KMS/HSM.
[45:30] Leah: i'll need a draft contract to review; can you send a sample T&C?
[45:36] Jordan: yes, we'll attach a standard enterprise contract and SOC2 report.
[50:10] Priya: ok great, thanks everyone.
[50:13] Jordan: thanks all	6 we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the benchmark.
[50:18] Carlos: Thanks. bye.

End of transcript.
